data.title: Wall Street’s Black Friday — Is a 2022-style crypto winter brewing?
data.description:
November is kicking off with unprecedented levels of market volatility.

The past 24 hours have been one big bloodbath. Tech stocks have been hit particularly hard. Over the last 24 hours, markets in the U.S, Japan, South Korea, China and Taiwan have combined to wipe $1.7 trillion off their market cap. This, after a flurry of earnings reports kicked off the “AI bubble” narrative again. 

The key takeaway? The market got a reality check. For instance, Alphabet lost more than 12% of its market value, highlighting just how quickly sentiment can turn when AI expectations collide with earnings reality.

However, it is the timing of this sell-off that is adding another layer of pressure to the crypto market.

According to the Kobeissi Letter, the probability of a Democratic sweep in next week’s U.S mid-term elections has risen by 7% to a record high of 72% over the last 2 days. This, as markets continue to accelerate their decline, adding another layer of macroeconomic uncertainty for the crypto market.

This leaves us with high rates, a falling stock market, $100+ oil prices, and rising CPI, PPI, and PCE inflation. Next week is going to be interesting, to say the least. 

However, the market isn’t entirely bearish just yet. 

Crypto’s 2022 playbook returns as market volatility builds

It’s been over a year since the October 2025 crash knocked down risk assets.

Bitcoin is still down over 30% from its pre-crash high of $126K. Considering the FUD surrounding U.S mid-terms, the Binance hack and recent tech sell-off, it seems the market still has a long way to go before any real recovery. This puts the question of whether crypto has found its bottom back in focus. 

Notably, the 2022 cycle could offer some clues. Back then, the FTX collapse was just about a year after BTC’s November 2021 high, lining up with the cycle bottom in late Q4 2022, when BTC dropped to $16K. What followed was a 155% rally, followed by another 120% run, pushing Bitcoin close to $108K by 2024.

So, could the ongoing volatility be setting crypto up for a 2022-style cycle?

Based on historical trends, Bitcoin falling below $80K and the overall market sell-off could allude to later phases of a crypto bottom. With macro uncertainty continuing to build, the market could be heading into the final stage of capitulation before a bounce back.

Thus, the risk-off trend will likely continue through year-end before the crypto sees a 2023-style uptrend.

Final Summary

data.title: Bitwise, Galaxy, and Morpho back CCI’s new framework for U.S crypto vault regulations
data.description:
The Crypto Council for Innovation (CCI) has proposed a new framework to bring crypto vaults under U.S securities laws.

In a 238-page report that was published on 29th October, the CCI outlined how regulators can assess different vault structures under existing securities regulations. This includes the Securities Act of 1933, the Investment Company Act of 1940, and the Investment Advisers Act of 1940.

90-year-old securities rules tested

For those unaware, crypto vaults are smart contracts that accept users’ token deposits and deploy them into financial strategies such as lending, borrowing, and investments to generate returns.

And, now their adoption is expanding beyond decentralized finance (DeFi), with traditional financial institutions also exploring their potential. In fact, according to S&P Global, assets deposited in vaults touched $131 billion in April 2026.

Hence, the CCI, along with members from Bitwise, Galaxy Digital, and Morpho, is arguing that crypto vaults should not automatically fall outside U.S federal securities laws just because they operate via blockchain technology and smart contracts.

Lending more weight to the proposal, Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley said,

Vaults are going to change capital markets. We’re delighted to get to be a part of it.

CCI’s dual framework for crypto vaults

In its detailed report, CCI came up with a two-sided ‘Control Framework’ to resolve how much authority human operators hold over deposited assets. Additionally, the framework would also sort out how much control investors have over their funds.

Additionally, the report examined four factors on the operator’s side, which included mandate, execution, governance, and disposition. Here, the report assessed whether operators can select investment strategies, reallocate capital, change protocol rules, or move deposited assets.

Meanwhile, for the depositor’s side, there were six conditions considered. These included, comprehensibility, verifiability, observability, predictability, notice, and actionability.

So, the crux here is simple, and that is CCI wants vaults with immutable smart contracts, transparent operations, limited human discretion, and permissionless withdrawals to face a different regulatory assessment from those where operators retain significant control over investment decisions.

CCI’s way of bringing regulatory clarity to crypto markets

Interestingly, the proposal also draws parallels with Section 10301 of the proposed CLARITY Act. For those unaware, the latter addressed non-decentralized finance protocols based on whether identifiable individuals or groups could control or materially alter their functionality.

And, therefore, the CCI wants regulators to adopt a similarly control-based approach. In fact, for regulatory clarity, CCI also wants the SEC to follow the approach it previously adopted for ETFs. This would involve granting individual exemptions to qualifying vault structures under Section 6(c) of the Investment Company Act before gradually introducing broader, standardized rules.

Commenting on the same, Horsley added,

We worked with regulators for years to help make crypto ETFs possible. We’re happy to collaborate again, this time on vaults.

The red flag in question

Needless to say, the proposal also echoes SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce’s 22nd July statement, Headstands and Summervaults, in which she cautioned, against treating all crypto vaults alike.

Vaults are not uniform

Here, it’s worth pointing out a recent report by AMBCrypto which highlighted how Web3 protocols are increasingly moving away from their original promises of openness, permissionlessness, and decentralization.

The report stressed on projects such as Hyperliquid, Aave, and Polygon that have adopted models that prioritize internal vaults, buybacks, and treasury accumulation over directly distributing value to token holders.

Final Summary

  • The CCI is arguing that crypto vaults should not automatically fall outside U.S federal securities laws.
  • According to S&P Global, assets deposited in vaults hit $131 billion in April 2026.

data.title: Why AAVE crypto traders must watch $113 support after Binance hack
data.description:
Around 9 pm UTC on the 29th of October, a Binance hot wallet on Ethereum sent 63 ERC-20 tokens and 167,464 ETH in a single transaction. The same exploiter address received another 28,006 ETH in a second transaction from a second Binance hot wallet on Ethereum, along with funds from Arbitrum [ARB], Optimism [OP], and Avalanche [AAVE].

In response, the Aave markets across all networks were frozen, stopping everyone, including the exploiter, from opening new supply or borrow positions.

The broader market has reacted bearishly, with Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH] down 3.46% and 3.93% in the past 24 hours, compared to Aave’s 5.67%. The crypto market witnessed over $1.50 billion in liquidations, with a majority being long liquidations.

Is the long-term AAVE trend bullish?

From June to September, the DeFi token rallied by 214.2%, from $60 to $188. Since making this local high, the altcoin has retraced by 32.9% to fall to $125.8.

The weekly trend was bearish, but there is some hope for the bulls that the current retracement could go towards $213-$240, provided the weekly session does not close below $113.4.

Swing traders looking to buy can do so in line with the daily chart, but should remember that the long-term trend was not in their favor.

Why AAVE traders must stay cautious!

The $140 support zone has been breached. The technical indicators on the daily timeframe were firmly bearish. At the same time, the swing structure was just about bullish.

The fair value gap around the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement level (white) at $129 was breached, and the bullish order block around $115 was being tested.

If the market-wide selling continues, it is highly likely Aave’s price structure would take a bearish shift. As things stand, swing traders can wait for a sign of demand, maybe in the form of heavy demand or a price move back above $120, to consider going long.

Final Summary

  • The Aave response to the Binance heist was to freeze their v3 and v4 markets, which was effective but also put selling pressure on the DeFi token and other related assets.
  • In this environment of fear, going long is risky. Swing traders can wait for a clearer conditions before looking for trading opportunities.

data.title: PYTH crypto sees $179M drop in secured value – Can prices recover?
data.description:
Pyth Network [PYTH] has recorded a massive decline over the past day, with the asset plummeting roughly 12% to a new local low at press time.

The reaction, expectedly, followed the Binance hack incident, which reportedly resulted in losses of roughly $6.3 billion. However, a closer look shows that the protocol has also recorded one of its weakest-performing months.

Perpetual market activity has further fueled the decline, as traders concentrate capital on shorting PYTH.

PYTH records a $179M capital outflow

The decline in PYTH was accompanied by a massive on-chain capital outflow, tracked through Total Value Secured (TVS).

TVS tracks the total value of assets managed by the protocol, including bridged and native tokens. The decline suggests that market participants are pulling back from active utility. Over the past day, TVS dropped from $3.164 billion to $2.985 billion, marking an outflow of $179 million in the past 24 hours as of writing .

More concerning is that Pyth Network’s earnings have also plummeted significantly over the past day, according to data from DeFiLlama. Earnings, which track gross profit after incentives, have fallen to roughly $1,310 at press time, the lowest level ever recorded on a monthly basis.

In fact, this represents a significant decline from September, when the protocol earned $434,640. When earnings drop to this level, it points to reduced protocol utility as users become more reluctant to engage with the platform.

Perpetual traders increase short positions

Sellers have dominated perpetual trading activity as they continue to expand their positions.

Funding Rate data for PYTH‘s perpetual market shows a significant concentration of short positions, with the rate falling to -0.0172 as of writing.

PYTH’s negative Funding Rate, now at an extreme level, shows that traders have positioned roughly $36.77 million in the perpetual market towards shorting the asset.

When broken down by trader category, the data shows that whales, traders who control large amounts of capital in the market, have been key participants influencing price dynamics.

The Whale-Retail Delta, which tracks the difference between whale and retail trading activity, rose to 0.301 over the past day as whale positioning in the asset continued to increase.

Spot traders accumulate despite the decline

Spot traders, despite the negative outlook, have been accumulating the asset.

According to CoinGlass, Spot Netflow tracks the inflow and outflow of capital on exchanges. When outflows exceed inflows, it suggests that more assets are being withdrawn from exchanges, potentially indicating accumulation.

Netflow currently stands at -$1.56 million, suggesting that following the decline, more capital has moved out of exchanges than into them. This outlook may stem from investors viewing the recent drop as a discount.

data.title: Why Celestia crypto’s breakdown below $0.47 could trigger more TIA losses
data.description:
Celestia [TIA] plunged 14.03% in 24 hours at press time, as fresh macroeconomic uncertainty triggered heavy selling across the altcoin market, deepening its recent losses.

This steep decline accompanied the Federal Reserve’s hawkish stance and persistent inflation concerns, which weakened demand for riskier altcoins.

Particularly, the Federal Reserve preserved its cautious monetary policy stance on the 28th of October. Additionally, September’s PCE inflation matched expectations at 3.6% annually, validating concerns about extended restrictive interest rates.

Despite the price decline, the token’s trading volume interestingly surged 38.04% to $72.72 million.

This divergence implied an elevated trading activity during the sell-off, even though the volume increase could not solely establish sellers’ dominance.

TIA traders retreat as Open Interest collapses

Celestia’s derivatives market registered a considerable contraction in trader exposure, beyond the spot market decline.

According to CoinGlass, TIA’s Open Interest (OI) dropped 28.60% to $75.86 million, suggesting that traders closed positions as the token’s price continued falling. The shrinking OI alone, however, could not distinguish voluntary position closures from forced liquidations.

Therefore, for Celestia, the depreciation emerged in the midst of a broader retreat in the speculative participation. As the derivatives positions diminished, the market encountered reduced leveraged exposure despite the increased trading activity.

Spot and Futures sellers tighten their grip

The bearish pressure notably extended across Celestia‘s spot and derivatives markets, confirming the weakness evident in its price performance.

As CryptoQuant analytics, TIA’s Spot Taker Cumulative Volume Delta (CVD) highlighted taker-sell dominance, implying aggressive sellers outweighed buyers executing market orders. Additionally, the Futures Taker CVD also showed taker-sell dominance, revealing similar behavior among the derivatives investors.

These readings together pointed towards a coordinated bearish pressure across the two markets. Noteworthy, unlike the falling OI, which implied declining outstanding positions, the CVD indicator highlighted the direction of aggressive trading.

The persistent selling across both markets therefore complicated TIA’s recovery attempts, and without a stronger buying participation, the token could struggle to reverse its recent losses.

TIA loses crucial support as bears advance

On the daily timeframe chart, Celestia’s price structure strengthened the bearish outlook after the token broke below the $0.4727 support level.

Notably, the price breakdown emerged after an earlier rejection around the $0.5548 zone, which had already weakened the token’s recovery structure.

The Parabolic SAR indicator, meanwhile, remained above the price at around $0.6616 as of press time, preserving its bearish signal.

Additionally, further weakness emerged from the RSI indicator, which fell to 39.44, remaining below its moving average, and suggesting deteriorating buying strength.

Consequently, the breakdown exposed the $0.3277 level as the next major support, even though buyers still had a better chance of intervening before that level.

A decisive reclaim of the $0.4727 resistance, however, could ease immediate selling pressure and reopen a recovery attempt toward the $0.5548 region.

Final Summary

  • Celestia plunged 14% as selling intensified and traders reduced their derivatives exposure.
  • TIA’s breakdown below $0.4727 raised the risk of further losses toward $0.3277.

data.title: Bitcoin whitepaper turns 18, but what are the challenges ahead for BTC’s $1.6T market?
data.description:
It has been 18 years since Satoshi Nakamoto’s Bitcoin whitepaper was released on 31st October, 2008. The idea was simple – Offer an exit hatch from the traditional financial system with a peer-to-peer (P2P) money network with a fixed supply (21M coins) and no central control. 

Interestingly, the timing was not coincidental. It was just over two months after the U.S government committed to bailing out major banks after the 2008 financial crisis using taxpayers’ money. 

That meant massive money printing and hyperinflation and a decline in citizens’ purchasing power and wealth. In fact, Satoshi captured this frustration in a message on the first genesis Bitcoin block, which he mined himself on 23rd January 2009. 

The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks.

18 years later, the banks Satoshi rebelled against are now adopting Bitcoin. Whether that is good or bad is debatable. Over the years, though, various narratives have shaped adoption and softened even some of Bitcoin’s once-vocal critics. 

What has changed after 2 decades?

Satoshi moved on to other things in early 2011, and BTC hit $1 that year. By 2025, the crypto’s price had rallied to a record $126K per coin on the back of increasing adoption by nation-states and companies as a sovereign global reserve asset. 

In fact, the world’s largest asset manager, BlackRock, initially labelled it a scam but later made a U-turn. In the last two years, BlackRock has pitched the $1.6T BTC market as digital gold and as a hedge against fiscal debt and geopolitical risks. 

Interestingly, U.S Spot BTC ETFs, led by BlackRock, now hold 1.6M BTC, the highest among institutional investors and nation-states. Public companies come in second at 1.265M BTC, with governments closing the top three list with 645.6K BTC. 

In particular, the UAE’s sovereign funds reported nearly $800M in BTC exposure in Q3, citing it as a strategic diversifier. This echoed BlackRock’s pitch.

As it stands, U.S fiscal debt is at +$40T and climbing. The EU and other jurisdictions are trying to stop P2P transfers. This has further cemented BTC’s original value proposition: a non-sovereign, censorship-resistant asset and hedge.  

In fact, even the BIS has acknowledged that BTC adoption highlights the level of distrust in traditional monetary systems and central banks. Interestingly, the BIS has called on central banks to modernize to counter BTC’s influence. 

Saumya Saxena, Global Builders Lead at Base, Coinbase, shared a similar position with AMBCrypto. 

Its (Bitcoin’s) significance goes beyond its scarcity; it represents a check and balance in the monetary system, demonstrating how competition can strengthen choice and trust.

What’s next for Bitcoin?

Right now, the network is facing security uncertainty from miners and post-quantum preparedness. Miners partly help secure the network, but their block rewards have dropped from 50 BTC to 3.125 BTC.

MARA thinks a further drop in rewards after the 2028 halving might make mining unsustainable.  

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin whitepaper turned 18 amid elevated fiscal debt, corruption, and geopolitical instability. 
  • Despite institutional adoption, Bitcoin faces security risks from miner exits and AI/quantum computer threats.

data.title: How Useless Coin’s 10% crash puts the $0.13 demand zone at risk
data.description:
Useless Coin [USELESS] has taken a big hit as the general crypto records a week of bearish advances. The token prices have dropped by more than 10% over the last 24 hours at press time, amid negative on-chain sentiments.

The token is trading below its key EMA and on the verge of breaking below the demand zone at around $0.13.

With the token leveraged position shrinking and significant unmitigated liquidity clusters lying below the current trading price, could the current bearish run be prolonged? 

Useless Coin faces mounting selling pressure

Useless Coin has followed the bearish trend witnessed across the majority of altcoins as they reap from the recent unchanged FOMC rates this week.

The token has since recorded significant bearish advances to test the current demand zone that sits between $0.125 and $0.145 as negative on-chain sentiment reinforces concerns about demand.

At the time of writing, the token was trading below all its key Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs) on the daily chart, leaving the short-term technical structure also tilted toward sellers. These EMAs could act as overhead resistance if the token attempts a recovery.

But with buyers having defended the zone on several occasions, this time it could follow the same trajectory. Notably, buyers have started to show up on short time frames.

Shrinking leveraged positions signals reduced volatility

On the derivatives, the token’s Open Interest has shrunk to just $32 million as of writing. This points to declining leveraged positions as traders and investors scale back their exposure as uncertainty increases.

At the same time, an unmitigated liquidity cluster worth $586K lies around 0.112. This highlights the price level as a key target for the network sellers before further bullish advances can be resumed.

In the past, similar zones acted as magnets to Useless’ price action. Moreover, the chances of the same repeating still remain high.

Can USELESS avoid further bearish push?

USELESS remains vulnerable while it trades below its key EMAs and tests the demand zone between $0.125 and $0.145. A successful defense could provide a base for recovery, particularly if broader market sentiment improves.

However, a decisive breakdown below $0.13 would strengthen the bearish outlook. Without renewed buying pressure, sellers could retain control and extend the decline.

As it stands, the $0.13 zone is the level to watch. Its ability to attract buyers could determine whether USELESS stabilizes or enters another phase of losses.

Final Summary

  • USELESS has dropped by more than 10% in the last 24 hours as negative on-chain sentiment and broader market weakness weigh on its price.
  • The network’s shrinking leveraged positions add to uncertainty as the token approaches the $0.13 demand zone, where a breakdown could expose it to further losses.

data.title: ‘Crypto moves forward regardless’ – Why Grayscale is looking past the U.S. midterms
data.description:
Grayscale’s Head of Research Zach Pandl believes that the cryptocurrency industry will continue to expand regardless of the outcome of the upcoming U.S. midterm elections.

In a report published on the 28th of October, Pandl argued that even if Democrats gain control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, the broader outlook for digital assets is unlikely to change significantly.

Zach Pandl’s bullish crypto market prediction

Currently, Republicans hold majorities in both chambers. However, prediction markets suggest that Democrats could take control after the elections.

Such a political shift could influence the regulatory environment for cryptocurrencies, particularly as the industry has benefited from greater regulatory clarity recently.

Furthermore, the years under Joe Biden offer sufficient evidence of a challenging cryptocurrency market. Despite this uncertainty, Pandl believes three major factors will support the industry’s long-term growth.

Factors driving Pandl’s prediction

According to Pandl, cryptocurrency is no longer associated with a single political party.

Research from Pew Research and The Harris Poll suggests that similar proportions of Republicans and Democrats own or use digital assets. Furthermore, legislation such as the GENIUS Act received bipartisan support in Congress, demonstrating that lawmakers from both parties recognize the importance of regulating and developing the sector.

He also highlighted the growing U.S. national debt as a long-term driver of cryptocurrency adoption. This is what Pandl believes would encourage investors to explore alternative stores of value, including Bitcoin [BTC] and other digital assets, as part of their broader investment strategies.

Main players in the U.S. crypto market

That said, Pandl also argued that the cryptocurrency industry does not depend exclusively on the United States. According to Grayscale’s estimates, only 15-20% of global crypto activity takes place in the U.S., while the remaining 80-85% happens internationally.

Hence, Pandl put it best when he said,

Regardless of the outcome of the US midterms, users around the world will continue to seek out alternatives to fiat currencies as well as more effective payment systems, and foreign regulators will continue to put in place rules to support digital assets innovation in their jurisdictions.

Crypto market dynamics paint a confusing picture

Well, the current crypto market dynamics also suggest the same, as the global cryptocurrency market capitalization stood at $2.71 trillion at press time, representing a 1.6% increase over the last 24 hours. Meanwhile, Bitcoin‘s market dominance stood at 60.30% at the time of reporting.

Additionally, the 24-hour trading volume reached $162.455 billion, up 120.9%. However, the market sentiment remains cautious as the Crypto Fear & Greed Index has dropped to 30, indicating ‘fear,’ compared with 51 (neutral) a day ago, 50 last week, and 71 (greed) last month.

This suggests that despite the increase in market capitalization, investors remain uncertain about near-term market conditions.

Lastly, AMBCrypto’s recent report also suggested that Bitcoin’s much-anticipated “Uptober” rally has disappointed investors, with BTC declining 4.2% month-to-date as of 25th October, against its historical average October return of 18.1%.

Still, all of these are mixed sentiments, which suggest that the market is still uncertain with no clear signs of what comes next.

Final Summary

  • At present, Republicans hold majorities in both chambers, but prediction markets suggest that Democrats could take control following the elections.
  • Only 15-20% of global crypto activity takes place in the U.S., while the remaining 80-85% happens internationally.

data.title: Can IMX bulls hold on after selling pressure fuels daily losses of 12%?
data.description:
As the market crashed on the back of Binance being hacked, most altcoins were left bleeding. Immutable was one of the most affected altcoins on the charts. In fact, IMX recorded a massive price drop on the charts. The altcoin not only lost the $0.12-support but also breached $0.11, dropping to a low of $0.106. 

Soon after, it slightly rebounded though. At the time of writing, Immutable was trading at around $0.11, down 12% on the daily charts.

At the same time, the altcoin’s volume jumped by 218%, hinting at strong selling pressure as traders reduced their exposure. The daily turnover further confirmed the selling pressure, with the same climbing to a three-week high of $5.06 million.

IMX plunges as sentiment flips risk-off

According to AMBCrypto, IMX’s fall was driven largely by weakness in the derivatives market. According to Coinalyze, Perpetual Sell Volume on Binance surged to 41 million, compared to 39 million in Buy Volume.

Perps bet buying fell deeper into the negative zone, falling to -6 million. This suggested that more positions were closed than open.

The same can be seen when examining the Futures flows. In fact, CoinGlass data revealed that Immutable’s Open Interest fell by 8.4%, dropping to $16.7 million.

This metric has not been this low since September. The drop was backed by higher volume as derivatives volume rose by 268% to $37 million.

A hike in volume and falling OI usually imply greater market activity as traders close positions to reduce risk exposure. Historically, risk-averse sentiment towards derivatives has led to short-term market shocks that often preceded price drops.

Spot market takes a different path

While derivatives traders panicked and risk sentiment flipped, spot investors increased their withdrawals. On 30th October, Immutable’s Spot Netflow dropped to -$0.4 million.

The rising withdrawals, especially following the Binance hack, suggested that most investors moved tokens off exchanges to either cold storage, private wallets, or other safer protocols.

However, this could mostly be interpreted as bullish for the altcoin as such withdrawals also reduced immediate selling pressure.

Lower supply helps in boosting scarcity and could help IMX recover from the recent slip on the price charts. 

Can IMX avoid slipping further?

With the market in panic mode, Immutable seemed to be under strong bearish pressure. A look at its momentum indicators seemed to confirm this view too.

For example, IMX’s Relative Strength Index (RSI) dropped to 26 into oversold territory. At the same time, the Relative Vigor Index (RVGI) formed a bearish crossover, falling deeper into the negative zone, further confirming the trend strength.

Taken together, these two indicators suggested that the momentum behind the downtrend is strong and that the trend is likely to continue. Therefore, if the sentiment persists after the Binance hack, IMX will revisit $0.10.

However, if the exchange outflows seen over the past day persist, they could help absorb some of the pressure. In doing so, the altcoin will close daily at $0.12, clearing the path for recovery.

Final summary

  • Immutable [IMX] fell by 12%, breached $0.12, falling to a low of $0.106 before rebounding slightly.
  • IMX’s fall was driven by intense selling pressure as derivatives sentiment turned risk off.

data.title: MARA stock slides 8% as Bitcoin retreats towards $76,500
data.description:
MARA Holdings shares fell 8.23% to $6.58 during the October 30 session, continuing the decline it’s been seeing in October. The Bitcoin miner’s stock fell as low as $6.44, its lowest level since 2023.

Bitcoin was also trading lower, near $76,714, as MARA’s recent price relationship with it strengthened.

October erases MARA’s September rebound

MARA approached $14 during September before seeing a sharp reversal. At the time of this writing, it had lost more than half its value from that peak.

A recent brief attempt to stay around the $7–$7.50 price area gave way to another decline on Friday. Shares opened at $6.81 and remained below that price at the time of this writing

The session was still underway, leaving the closing price unsettled.

The chart’s moving averages also slope downward above the stock. What this shows is that MARA is trading well below its recent average prices, and its earlier recovery attempts have not helped it to reverse the broader decline.

Bitcoin’s retreat provides context

The comparison chart placed Bitcoin near $76,714 and had reached $76,500 during the ongoing session.

Bitcoin’s decline followed a retreat from around $87,000 in September and early October. The latest selling took it below the $80,000–$82,000 area, where it traded recently.

MARA’s chart showed a 20-period correlation reading of positive 0.78 against BTCUSDT. That indicates a strong positive relationship between their closing-price levels over the selected daily window.

The reading helps to show their recent connection.

Their displayed daily percentage changes also cover different trading windows, since Bitcoin trades continuously and MARA follows stock-market hours.

What would stabilization look like?

Friday’s low of $6.44 would be the first nearby zone MARA should be looking at. If MARA can continue trading below that level, it would extend the decline into new lows. It is worth noting here that MARA share price has not been at the lows we are seeing since March 2023.

If it could push back past $7, then this would be pulling above levels it has been comfortable with lately. Some consolidation in the $7; $7.50 area for the next few days could bring some sense that this most recent slide is losing its steam.

Bitcoin’s nearby reference sits around $76,500, close to its 200-day average. A level to watch if selling does continue is around the 75k low range found in previous sessions.

Both charts still show limited recovery from their latest falls, leaving the next closing prices important to see whether buyers can establish firmer ground.

Final Summary

  • MARA traded at $6.58, down 8.23%, after reaching a fresh low since 2023.
  • Its recent closing-price correlation with Bitcoin was at 0.78 as BTC traded near $76,700.
